summary: Carson NF lookout on San Antonio Mountain: planned by 1911, lightning-struck cabin in 1918; listed gone, no removal date found.

facts.design: Lookout cabin with a short tower attached (NRHP nomination). A 1918 newspaper item describes a one-floor house about 12 by 12 feet with walls almost wholly of glass. The accounts do not match.
facts.status_note: Listed as gone on the Forest Fire Lookout Association list. No source dates its removal or describes the lookout site now; the summit has radio and television towers.

staffing.status: lookoutman in the house when lightning struck the cabin, June 18, 1918

access.note: On Carson National Forest land on San Antonio Mountain. Wikipedia says Forest Road 418 has a locked gate where it crosses private property and may not be open to motorized travel by the general public.

facts.agency: USDA Forest Service, Carson National Forest

events.note: A line was to be built to San Antone Mountain, where a lookout station for forest fires would be established. The item is a plan; it does not say when the station was finished.
Lookoutman Mr. Ground was in the lookout house on the night of June 18, 1918.
Lightning struck the cabin on the night of June 18, 1918 and tore a hole two feet square in the roof. The lookoutman was not hurt.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The NRHP nomination describes a short tower attached to a log cabin. The 1918 newspaper item describes a one-floor house about 12 by 12 feet with walls almost wholly of glass. The sources do not say whether these describe the same building or different periods, so the story reports both and does not choose.

notes_for_editor: Sparse record: two newspaper items (1911 plan, 1918 incident) quoted on a hobby site, one NRHP sentence, and the FFLA list. The 1911 item describes a plan, so no build date is recorded. The NRHP sentence's date phrase is garbled in the cached copy ('early 19BOs'), so it is not used. Removal date unknown. Summit radio towers and road gate come from Wikipedia; a USFS or Carson NF source would be better before publication. Record county Rio Arriba and the coordinates fit the summit area.
